Subject: RE: Acme MSA — term & renewal language (prep)

Team — quick sync before we send the next redline to Acme. They flagged three hot items in their last call: (1) automatic renewal notice window, (2) termination for convenience and any associated fees, and (3) what happens to cached data after termination.

Summary of my read: our standard is 30-day opt-out notice for auto-renew, no termination-for-convenience fee (we typically allow either party to terminate with 60 days’ notice but no penalty), and 90 days of platform access for customers to export data after termination. Acme wants longer notice windows (60–90 days) and an explicit termination-for-convenience payment equal to 10% of remaining committed fees if they terminate early.

Requested actions: 
- Laura: can you propose defensible language that keeps notice at 30 days but gives flexibility for 60 days on a per-deal basis? Also confirm our stance on termination-for-convenience fees (we generally avoid them for self-serve deals but for committed Reserved capacity we can negotiate a ramp-down fee).
- Karthik & Vanessa: I want a short blurb for the customer framing why 30 days is standard and how we can offer a compromise for Dedicated/Reserved bookings.
- Stephanie: confirm data access timing and any operational constraints if we extend export window beyond 90 days.

Attachments: I pulled together a one-pager of options and included the draft redline (v3) with inline comments.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas / team — see proposed language below and attached redline (Acme_MSA_redline_v3.docx). I tried to balance commercial flexibility with risk control. Key points: 

1) Auto-renewal / Notice window (Section 3.2): 
Proposed: "Unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the then-current Term end date, the Term will automatically renew for successive one (1) year terms; provided, however, that for Reserved Capacity commitments, Customer may elect an extended notice window of up to sixty (60) days by written agreement at the time of signing."
Rationale: preserves our standard while allowing explicit per-deal variation for reserved capacity.

2) Termination for convenience (Section 7.3): 
Proposed: "Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. If Customer terminates for convenience during a Reserved Capacity Commitment Period, Customer shall pay a termination fee equal to ten percent (10%) of the remaining, unpaid portion of the committed fees, unless otherwise agreed in writing."
Rationale: aligns with our existing billing and preserves ability to negotiate a fee for committed capacity. Keeps it symmetric which is important for risk allocation.

3) Post-termination access and data (Section 9.1): 
Proposed: "Upon termination, Customer retains read-only access to its account and stored data for a period of up to ninety (90) days for export; Customer may request an additional extension of up to an additional ninety (90) days for which Redwood will provide export assistance for a negotiated fee."
Rationale: provides a standard 90-day window and a paid extension path to avoid long tail operational burden.

I noted Acme's previous comment about a 'longer grace period if we are mid-migration' — we can offer a one-time six (6) month extension for enterprise migrations but only if the order form explicitly references migration timeline and commits to a Reserved Capacity minimum.

If you want I can mark up a short paragraph for Karthik to include in outbound framing.

Laura

Subject: Proposed MSA redline and termination compromise

Sara — thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is our next redline (Acme_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a short one-pager (Termination_Summary_onepager.pdf) that explains the commercial tradeoffs. High level: we kept the auto-renew notice at 30 days by default but added explicit language to allow 60-day notice for Reserved Capacity bookings. We also proposed symmetric termination-for-convenience with a 60-day notice and a 10% fee only if the termination is of a Reserved Capacity commitment.

Why this should work for Acme: 
- Predictability: shorter notice keeps renewal cycles tight (helps both sides plan), but the 60-day option gives you runway for Reserved capacity decisions.
- Fairness: termination fee only kicks in where we've provisioned dedicated capacity or committed discounts.
- Data continuity: 90 days read-only export window plus a paid extension path for migrations.

Please review the redline and let us know which of the three sections you'd like to discuss further. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with Laura and Jonas to walk through the language.

Karthik / team — thanks for the updated redline and the one-pager, helpful framing. A few quick notes from Acme Legal after internal review (high level):

1) Notice window: Acme is willing to accept 30 days for standard renewals but requests a minimum 60-day notice for renewal notices related to "Committed Capacity". We are comfortable with Redwood's per-deal carve for Reserved Capacity but want the baseline language to say: "for Committed Capacity, notice shall be no less than sixty (60) days."

2) Termination-for-convenience fee: Acme cannot accept a customer-only fee. If a fee is to exist for early termination of committed capacity, it must be mutual (i.e., apply to either party) or be tied to demonstrable provisioning costs (we're open to a ramp-down schedule tied to a fixed cost table rather than a flat percentage).

3) Data export period: 90 days is okay for standard accounts, but for migrations we need at least 180 days or a defined migration assistance plan (SOW). If Redwood wants a paid extension, we prefer a cap on fees and a clear SLA for assistance.

We'd like to schedule a 45-minute call next week with Laura and Jonas to finalize language. Also attached is our annotated counter (Acme_MSA_counter_v2.pdf) with inline comments — for speed I can pull out the three disputed paragraphs and propose line edits on the call.

Thanks — Sara

On a related note, procurement asked if we can get the Order Form finalized by Feb 15 to start provisioning.
